claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your circumstances.

Let me start with a few questions:

**First, could you tell me: How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for your help. I'm inquiring about my child Alex, who is 7 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about **Alex, who is 7 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, that's good - they fall within the standard Child Benefit age range. Now I need to understand your living situation and responsibility for Alex.

**Could you tell me: Do you live with Alex, or what is your living arrangement with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that. Since Alex lives with you at home, that helps establish responsibility.

Now I need to check a few more important details about your circumstances to determine eligibility.

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK - I currently live abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Living abroad can affect Child Benefit eligibility, but there are some circumstances where you may still be able to claim.

**Could you tell me: What country do you currently live in?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not say exactly which country, but I'm living outside the UK at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. That's helpful context. To determine if you might still be eligible for Child Benefit while living abroad, I need to ask:

**Are you a Crown servant (such as working for the UK government, Foreign Office, or similar)? Or do you have any other specific connection to the UK government's employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't work for the UK government or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since you live abroad and are not a Crown servant, I need to understand your immigration status in the UK, as this affects Child Benefit eligibility for people living outside the UK.

**Do you have settled status or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't have settled or pre-settled status.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me so far:

- You have a child, Alex, who is 7 years old
- Alex lives with you
- You currently live abroad (outside the UK)
- You are not a Crown servant
- You do not have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme

According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and **you live in the UK**. 

Since you're living abroad and don't fall into the exceptions (Crown servant or EU Settlement Scheme status), this means you would not be eligible for Child Benefit at this time.

However, before I provide my final assessment, let me confirm one more thing:

**If you were to move back to the UK, would you have the right to reside in the UK?** This is important because even if you move back, you'd need to have the right to reside there to claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I understand. Yes, if I moved back to the UK, I would have the right to reside there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's useful information for the future, though it doesn't change your current situation since you're living abroad now.

Based on all the information you've provided, I can now provide you with my eligibility assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

**You are not currently eligible for Child Benefit** because you live abroad. 

While you meet the other requirements (Alex is under 16 and lives with you), Child Benefit requires you to live in the UK. The exceptions that allow people to claim while living abroad are:
- Being a Crown servant, or
- Having settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme

Since neither of these applies to you, you cannot claim at the moment.

**Good news:** If you were to move back to the UK in the future, you've confirmed you would have the right to reside there, which means you would then be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex. When that happens, you can make a new claim.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
